original_question: For the extension in which conflict memories are generated from nonlocal conflict encounters through a top-hat detection kernel, determine whether time-dependent solutions exist in a bounded periodic domain.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 17 in §2.2.2: "In what sense do solutions exist solving the time-dependent problem (2.16) subject to periodic boundary conditions and a top-hat detection function in a bounded domain?"
correct_elements: The draft correctly targets the new extension of the conflict-memory model in which conflict memories are generated by nonlocal conflict encounters, keeps the top-hat detection kernel, and focuses on existence of time-dependent solutions in a bounded periodic setting. Those are the core ingredients of Open Problem 17.
missing_details: The draft does not identify the exact target as Open Problem 17 for model (2.16), the specific extension of the conflict-zone memory model (2.13).
It omits the full coupled system: the population-density equations for u_i and the cognitive-map equations for k_i.
It does not say that the model concerns n interacting populations indexed by i = 1, ..., n.
It omits the perception/convolution notation a^{g,R}(x,t) = integral over the domain of a(y,t) g_R(x-y) dy, and in particular the quantities k_i^{g,R} and u_i^{g,R} that appear in (2.16).

It does not specify the parameter roles and restrictions used in the nearby context: diffusion rates d_i > 0, repulsion/advection rates gamma_i >= 0, encounter rates rho_ij >= 0, memory-decay rate mu >= 0, conflict-zone decay parameter beta >= 0, and perceptual radius R >= 0.

It does not define the top-hat detection kernel itself: in §2.1 the paper gives the one-dimensional top-hat kernel g_R(x-y) = 1/(2R) for |x-y| <= R and 0 otherwise, and notes the higher-dimensional normalized-ball analogue.
It does not state that this extension assumes the same perceptual kernel and perceptual radius for each population.
It does not make explicit that the bounded periodic setting means periodic boundary conditions on a bounded domain, equivalently the torus viewpoint in higher dimensions.

It does not reflect the paper's exact phrasing "in what sense do solutions exist," which leaves open the appropriate solution concept, regularity class, and local/global existence framework rather than asking only for a yes/no answer.

To stay paper-faithful, the question should exclude neighboring issues not asked in Open Problem 17, such as nonconstant steady states (Open Problem 18), comparison with the local-conflict model (Open Problem 19), or nonperiodic boundary conditions (Open Problem 20).
refined_question:
Let Omega be a bounded domain equipped with periodic boundary conditions (equivalently, a flat torus in higher dimensions), let g_R be the top-hat detection kernel of perceptual radius R, and let a^{g,R}(x,t) denote the corresponding periodic perception operator. For n interacting populations u_i(x,t) with conflict-memory variables k_i(x,t), consider the nonlocal-conflict-zone extension of the conflict-memory model given by
∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i + gamma_i ∇·(u_i ∇k_i^{g,R}),
∂_t k_i = u_i^{g,R} sum_{j=1}^n rho_ij u_j - (mu + beta u_i) k_i,
for i = 1, ..., n, where d_i > 0, gamma_i >= 0, rho_ij >= 0, mu >= 0, beta >= 0, and the same top-hat kernel g_R and perceptual radius R are used for each population. In what sense do time-dependent solutions to this system exist on Omega under periodic boundary conditions?
justification: The draft is closest to Open Problem 17, not to Open Problems 10 or 15, because §2.2.2 first introduces the local conflict-zone memory model (2.13) and then, in the nearby "New models and extensions" discussion, replaces local conflict encounters by nonlocal ones, yielding model (2.16). Immediately after this, the paper asks exactly for existence of time-dependent solutions to (2.16) under periodic boundary conditions with a top-hat detection function in a bounded domain. Section 2.1 supplies the definition of the top-hat kernel and the notation a^{g,R} for the perception operator. Section 4.1.2 explains what the periodic bounded-domain setting means and why the paper emphasizes periodic problems for nonlocal kernels. Section 5.1.1 clarifies why the wording is "in what sense do solutions exist": the top-hat kernel is discontinuous, making standard well-posedness theory difficult to apply directly.
